Awards Night
A five-star ballroom. Chandeliers, cameras, the whole team in borrowed suits. The host announces: "Emerging Player of the Series."
And to present it: "Mr. Raghav Mehra."
A boy from a chai stall. Look at him now. I always say: this game rewards those who understand how it works.
He hands you the trophy. He doesn't let go of it. He leans in, smiling for the cameras.
You ran at ball three. I'll remember that. Rajgarh will remember it too.
Take the microphone. Say it all. Live.
In front of every camera in the country.
Smile. Take the trophy. Let Rathore finish it quietly.
The careful way.
You turn to the microphone. The room goes silent the way a stadium goes silent before a big appeal.
Papa sells chai, not wickets.
You say everything. Jassi, Karan, the fire, ball three. Mehra laughs. "A talented boy with a vivid imagination. My lawyers will be in touch."
Without the proof in your hands, it's your word against a billionaire's. The cameras cut away.
You say everything. Then Rathore stands up at table nine and plays it through the ballroom speakers. His voice. His instructions. Ball three.
Turn that off. TURN IT OFF.
Four officers in plain clothes walk across the ballroom. The cameras don't cut away. Not one.
You smile. You take the trophy. At 2 AM, Rathore calls.
Not enough. His lawyers will eat it.
We'll keep watching. So will he.
Arrested at the airport. 1:40 AM. Trying to board his own jet.
No cameras. Your way was quieter. It worked.
Our boy. So sensible. I knew you would understand how the game works.
Rathore stands behind you, not unkindly, and puts a hand on your shoulder.
We'll talk after the dinner, {first}. Bring your phone.
Raghav Mehra walks out of the ballroom smiling. "See you next season, champ."
In handcuffs, Raghav Mehra laughs. "You think I'm the top of this? I'm a branch manager."
